facts.raw_span: asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face that had progressively spread to the trunk and extremities
asthenia and mild intermittent arthralgias
Multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules involving the head, trunk, and extremities
Symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples
No vesicles or pustules
Normal white blood cell count
Mild anemia (hemoglobin level, 11.3 g/dL; normal level 12.50-15.50 g/dL)
Hypocomplementemia
Moderate proteinuria
Raised levels of antinuclear antibodies (>1:160)
Positive: anti-Smith antibodies, SSA/Ro antibodies, SSB/La antibodies, and anti-U1RNP antibodies
Slightly atrophic epidermis with interface dermatitis, individual dyskeratotic keratinocytes, and a superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of neutrophils

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of cutaneous lesions, asthenia, and arthralgias, along with laboratory findings of raised antinuclear antibodies and specific autoantibodies, are consistent with Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including mild anemia, hypocomplementemia, and moderate proteinuria, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

The patient's cutaneous lesions, including millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques, are consistent with Discoid Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including asthenia, arthralgias, mild anemia, and raised antinuclear antibodies, are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.

rationales.F01: Asymptomatic cutaneous lesions are common in various lupus conditions, making this finding neutral.
rationales.F02: Asthenia and arthralgias are more commonly associated with systemic lupus and mixed connective tissue disease.
rationales.F03: Keratotic papules are characteristic of subacute cutaneous lupus.
rationales.F04: Annular plaques on the cheeks and temples are characteristic of subacute cutaneous lupus.
rationales.F08: Hypocomplementemia is often seen in lupus conditions, particularly systemic lupus.
rationales.F10: Raised antinuclear antibodies are highly suggestive of lupus conditions.
rationales.F11: Specific autoantibodies like anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, and SSB/La are highly indicative of lupus conditions, particularly subacute cutaneous lupus and systemic lupus.
rationales.F12: Histopathological findings of interface dermatitis and specific infiltrates are characteristic of lupus conditions, particularly subacute cutaneous lupus.
